Instinctively we're looking for the "Edit note" label and expect it to be higher up in the context menu where the second section is in the context menu. 
The team agrees that since we have "delete note" in the edit panel that we're comfortable removing this from the context menu and to have "Edit note" as the primary action. 

We would also want "Add note" to be in the same new position for consistency.

Wanted to get your thoughts on the proposed update. Thanks!

@Amy Lee I see that the style for the screenshot is slightly different, with the rounded corners and the padding around the image (previously it extended across the full width). I have a couple questions about this.

1: Are we ok with changing this independently of Tab Notes? i.e. if we land this in Nightly without doing extra work to gate these styles behind the tab notes pref, everyone will see the new style, even if they don't have tab notes enabled. This seems reasonable to me, but I wanted to check with you to see if we are ok with this.

2: I noticed that in the new spec, the image is slightly smaller to account for the padding. This causes a small engineering issue. These screenshots are generated at a fixed size (280x140px) and used in a few different places (like Ctrl+Tab). If the size of the thumbnail shrinks here, we have to basically shrink the size of the generated image by a few pixels in CSS. If we do this, in some cases the antialiasing will cause the screenshot to appear blurry. I can post an example if you want to see what I mean.

The simplest way to fix this would be to make the panel slightly larger to keep the screenshot the same size while also adding the padding. We discussed this in standup yesterday but didn't want to decide without your input.
@Jeremy Swinarton – Can we still have the character limit when the user is adding the note if we are defining the limit by line length?

@Jeremy Swinarton – Hi, here is the max characters section. Since you can only specify lines and not characters we can limit the line length to 10 lines. I'm wondering how does that work if we want to have a 1000 character limit message show up? CC @Laura Lopez

@Amy Lee hey, I can't seem to find it in the spec doc, but on the bug for showing the note in the tab preview panel, it is specifed that the truncated version should show 350 characters. In CSS, the simplest way to truncate is by number of lines, not by character length. Is it ok if we specify it this way, maybe truncating after 8 or so lines?

@Amy Lee @Ania Safko Jeremy suggested that we allow the user to paste more than 1k characters, but disable the save button until the user edits the message below 1k characters. This sounds better than truncating the user's text ourselves.

I think the juice isn't worth the squeeze to figure out to this should work, write the strings, design, maintain - I'd focus on the higher viz spots above.

Similar to my comment on the call-out, I'd simplify the headline a bit to focus on core functionality and brevity: 

New: tab notes and names 
Right-click any tab to add a note. Double click to rename it.
Is this when a user taps on their current tab, or a different one? Wondering if the former use case is a common enough one to trigger enough messages.

Based on content here, my thinking is that the message bar isn't adding new info they can't understand from the experience itself. Explaining that something is linked to a tab vs. URL is probably too heady, too. 

As for saving automatically?, they probably assume that or we should communicate that visually.

Where do they get saved? Is it in the overflow or app menu? Might be helpful to name the location. I also wonder if this is a "Show me how" moment - Emily did a message recently that has a functionality of opening the app menu. This could be a great opportunity for that.

Since marketing will write this, I'd probably use less realistic copy: "Headline about new tab features goes here". I think I am suggesting that because I wonder if "never forget a tab" is the real value prop - is this what resonated? (but also don't want you to have to spend a ton of time on this since you aren't writing it ultimately) =)
Would "Tabs" be a new item in the app menu? It's not there today

I know you mentioned that tab renaming is a smaller feature but I also suspect it could be even more popular than a tab note. Talking about both within one call-out is too much, I think. I'd opt for two distinct call-outs or a tour... is it possible to have the tour be disconnected messages? ie, they don't layer and instead appear anchored on different pieces of UI?

My inclination is to keep the headline quite tight and simplify because we know people don't or won't want to read much and because our winning PDF call-out named the feature in the headline. Riff: 

Add a note to this tab 
[More detailed copy about the value prop or functionality]

@Ania Safko – Tried an option here based on the PRD ask. This is not my preference. It feels like the user needs to do an extra step to try the feature out. There's the idea of onboarding fatigue where you don't want to go through a multi step process and it forces you to make a decision where you might just want to try the feature out without a specific goal in mind. There's also little benefit to the difference between a work/personal list besides a different label (which will probably be generic. 

I like the previous option where the user can jump right in and drag and drop a tab to see what happens. It feels more light weight with less barriers. CC @Laura Lopez

@Ania Safko @Laura Lopez – A modal prompting the user if they want to check off a task. 

Concerns: Do we prompt this every time a user closes a tab linked to a task? 

If we want to have a "never show" again checkbox, we will end up with 2 checkboxes here. The options feel overwhelming.

Also an overlay feels a bit of an overkill for this scenario. Thoughts?

@Ania Safko – This wasn't in the brief but an optional "add current tab" function.

Some edge cases would be:
• Do we let the user add multiple instances of the current tab or disable the function if they just added the tab?

Edge case: 
If the user adds a current tab and then scrolls to another position on the webpage do we allow the user to add another instance of it?

I feel like we should let the user decide. If they want to add multiple copies of the same thing, is there a reason we shouldn't let them?

Also wording: 
"Add current tab" – Sounds like we're adding the tab and not the webpage URL. Do users care about this nuance? Thoughts @Laura Lopez?

My gut reaction is that task or to-do makes the most sense, because if I convert a tab to something I can check off, it's because I want to specifically treat it like an action I can clear. For reminder, I can leave the tab open to remind me and it's more passive. Follow up feels too narrow, and action feels too generic.
